newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes sharply higher late, fear low stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes sharply higher late, fear low stocks.

text.p: U.S. crudes held onto gains after the market stampeded higher on renewed concerns of low product stocks this winter and tight imports.
Sentiment was already nervous in early trade after news of fighting in Iraq's Kurdish northern region, and from a weekend fire at BP's Toledo, Ohio refinery.
November West Texas Intermeidate/Cushing rose to $25.45-55 a barrel, 85 cents firmer than late Friday.
Traders said a mixture of concerns over heating oil stock shortages, in spite of high refinery runs, was inspiring most to take on length going into the fourth quarter.
A firming in the Nov/Dec WTI spread by 10 cents to 40-42 cents, triggered demand for WTI/Cushing Posting Plus which saw the grade trade from postings plus $2.03 to $2.12.
But some domestics eased from intraday highs as buyers refrained in the wake of a sharp jump in outright prices.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded several times at WTI plus 63-65 cents, but eased to plus 60 cents later.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire inched to 49 cents a barrel, up five cents from last week.
Sweet grades remain popular alternatives to North Sea and West African crudes, currently in short supply.
Traders said speculation a ULCC fixed on subjects from Sullom Voe to the U.S. may be diverted elsewhere, causing delivered Brent to stay expensive, helped domestics.
Sour grades were barely changed with only one trade seen for Eugene Island at WTI minus $1.04, within Friday's range.
More supplies of competing sours from Latin America and upcoming cargoes from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve should keep a lid on Gulf Coast sour differentials, traders said.
